root_cause.text: The asd_pci_remove() function frees the asd_ha structure without first synchronizing pending tasklets, allowing tasklet handlers to access freed memory after device removal.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `tasklet_kill(&asd_ha->seq.dl_tasklet)` immediately after `asd_disable_ints(asd_ha)` and before resource cleanup in asd_pci_remove(). This synchronization point ensures all scheduled tasklets complete their execution before the asd_ha structure is freed, preventing the race condition where a tasklet could dereference the freed structure during device removal or module unload.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent use-after-free by killing the download tasklet before freeing device resources during PCI device removal.
intent_record.what: Added a call to tasklet_kill(&asd_ha->seq.dl_tasklet) in the asd_pci_remove function, preceded by a comment explaining the purpose of ensuring scheduled tasklets complete before resource cleanup.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that any pending tasklet execution is terminated and allowed to complete before the device removal process continues to free other resources. Without this, a tasklet could attempt to access freed memory or resources, causing use-after-free bugs or crashes during device removal.

      o aic94xx: disable split co
bic_trace_step.reason: The asd_pci_remove() function (lines 799-825) frees the asd_ha structure without synchronizing pending tasklets. The function calls asd_free_queues() (line 819) which handles pending work, but there is no call to tasklet_kill() or tasklet_disable() to synchronize any tasklets that may be running. The vulnerability root cause states that tasklet handlers can access freed memory after device removal. Looking at the removal sequence: asd_unregister_sas_ha() (line 805), asd_disable_ints() (line 807), free_irq() (line 815), asd_destroy_ha_caches() (line 821), asd_unmap_ha() (line 822), and kfree(asd_ha) (line 823) - none of these operations include tasklet synchronization. The code lacks any tasklet_kill() or similar synchronization mechanism before freeing the asd_ha structure, which is the vulnerable construct described in the root cause.
